source.title: Textually Pretrained Speech Language Models
source.authors: Michael Hassid; Tal Remez; T. Nguyen; Itai Gat; Alexis Conneau; F. Kreuk; Jade Copet; Alexandre Défossez; Gabriel Synnaeve; Emmanuel Dupoux; Roy Schwartz; Yossi Adi

record.tranche_reason: The study extends model- and data-scaling experiments to speech language models and reports speech-token perplexity and benchmark performance. It does not reproduce the original text-LM scaling-law fits.
record.gate_note: The study reports speech perplexity across model sizes and training-data fractions, plus zero-shot speech and spoken StoryCloze benchmark results across model sizes. It does not fit power laws or report scaling exponents. Results about warm initialization, speech tokenizers, human generation ratings, resynthesis, and image-model initialization are not rows unless they directly report the scaled measures recorded here.
record.test_reason: The study trains speech-token LMs at three sizes (125M–1.3B) and three data fractions (1/10/100%), plus 7B/13B models. It reports held-out speech PPL and zero-shot benchmark scores, so it bears on V5 and V6 in a new modality. It fits no power laws, so only the direction of scaling is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The main conclusion is that warm-starting SpeechLMs from text LMs (TWIST) beats cold start on all metrics. Secondarily, the authors find that model and data scale both improve SpeechLMs 'in almost all cases'. They fit no scaling law.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales speech-token language models and evaluates speech PPL and speech benchmarks; it does not reproduce the original text-LM scaling-law methodology. It reports sparse size/data sweeps rather than fitted scaling curves.
record.method_sensitivity: Results are reported across different model sizes, training-data fractions, speech token counts and token frequencies, and initialization methods. The study notes that tokenizer frequency affects benchmark results.
record.problems: The scaling sweeps are sparse, cover a limited range of model sizes and data fractions, and do not fit power laws or report uncertainty for the scaling metrics. Some low-data PPL comparisons are non-monotonic with model size.
record.rows_left_out: Table 7 also reports sWUGGY and sBLIMP for every model, data fraction, and tokenizer configuration; those additional scaling-metric rows were omitted to keep the record within the 60-row limit. The corresponding larger-model benchmark scores and StoryCloze size comparisons are retained in Tables 3 and 4. Other non-scaling results are not included.

untested.parts: Power-law form, exponents and range over several orders of magnitude (parameters span only about 1 order in the controlled sweep). Image/video, repeated-data laws and compute scaling were not tested.
Predictability (no fit of downstream score vs scale or loss), and the relation of downstream score to pretraining loss.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.

missing.what: Text-PPL of transcribed generations, which is non-monotone in size: 350M is worse than 125M (cold 117.17 vs 88.17)
Human MMOS ratings rising with scale (Cold-1.3B 3.34, TWIST-1.3B 3.51, TWIST-7B 3.79 on LS-clean)
Table 7 sWUGGY values, declared left out. At 1% data they fall with size (cold 66.90→64.91), and 350M TWIST full data equals 10% data (79.44 vs 81.23). These bear on V6 non-monotonicity.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The controlled sweep has only 3 sizes by 3 data fractions, with the checkpoint selected by validation PPL. The 1% data runs see heavy repetition, so size-increases there reflect data bottleneck. The 7B/13B models use LLaMA init and a different schedule, so their comparison with 1.3B confounds scale with recipe.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test power-law loss scaling for text language models.
No small-run fit is used to predict much larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between parameters and tokens is evaluated.
The study does not compare depth or width at a fixed parameter count.
The study examines speech models, not image or video models, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer. It reports no power-law fits, exponents, or tests over several orders of magnitude.
It reports zero-shot speech metrics and spoken StoryCloze accuracy across model sizes, but does not test a general downstream-task scaling law or relate downstream performance to pretraining loss.
The study does not compare fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits across fitting choices.

relationships.condition: Speech-token LMs (HuBERT tokens), cold and text-warm-started, 125M–1.3B at 10% and 100% data; plus 7B/13B
relationships.reason: Held-out speech PPL falls monotonically with size in every tokenizer/init group (t7-*-1300-c100, t7-*-1300-w100, t7-*-1300-c10, t3-7-ppl, t3-13-ppl). This supports direction only; the power-law form is not shown.
relationships.display_finding: Held-out speech perplexity decreased monotonically with size in every tokenizer and initialization group, without establishing a power-law form.

relationships.condition: TWIST 1.3B→7B→13B on sWUGGY, sBLIMP and Topic StoryCloze
relationships.reason: Scores rise with size: sWUGGY all 72.7→73.9→74.5 and TSC 70.6→74.1→76.4 (t3-7-sw-all, t3-13-sw-all, t4-tsc-*). Size steps are confounded with a change of base model and recipe.
relationships.display_finding: sWUGGY scores increased through 72.7, 73.9, and 74.5 and Topic StoryCloze through 70.6, 74.1, and 76.4, with backbone and training recipe changes confounded with size.

relationships.reason: SSC gains only 0.1 point (55.3→55.4) and sBLIMP 0.2 point from 7B to 13B (t4-ssc-13, t3-13-sb). Gains flatten on harder tasks.
relationships.display_finding: Spoken StoryCloze increased only from 55.3 to 55.4, while sBLIMP gained just 0.2 points.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Speech SpeechLM scaling sweep in Table 7 and larger models in Table 3
reader_labels.reason: The speech-token PPL sweep is sparse and contains increases with model size in some low-data settings; the study reports no power-law fits or exponents (rows t7-200-125-c, t7-200-350-c, t7-200-1300-c, t7-500-125-c, t7-500-350-c, t7-500-1300-c, t3-13-ppl, t3-7-ppl).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: TWIST models evaluated at 1.3B, 7B, and 13B on speech metrics and spoken StoryCloze
reader_labels.reason: Reported zero-shot speech scores and both spoken StoryCloze scores rise across the evaluated larger TWIST models (rows t3-13-sw-all, t3-13-sw-in, t3-13-sb, t3-7-sw-all, t3-7-sw-in, t3-7-sb, t4-ssc-13, t4-tsc-13, t4-ssc-7, t4-tsc-7, t4-ssc-13b, t4-tsc-13b).
